thread:
Maya (People Ops): thanks all for joining the all-hands Q&A. Recording + notes: https://confluence.redwood/all-hands/midyear-2026. key follow-ups below — dropping short answers to the common questions.
Alec (Eng): quick one: eligibility window for mid-year promotions? half the team thought it was only for folks hired before march.
Maya (People Ops): eligibility: anyone with >=6 months tenure by the end of the cycle is eligible. hiring date cutoff = the day before cycle close (see schedule). exceptions for contractors are handled case-by-case.
Priya (SWE): will performance ratings change? we use them for calibrations so want to know the rubric.
Maya (People Ops): ratings are same framework but we added clearer "sustained impact" guidance. no forced curve changes. rubric link: https://redwood.company/people/rubric-v2 (internal).
Laila (Manager): about comp pool: is there a firm % budget for raises this cycle? teams are planning comp conversations.
Maya (People Ops): comp pool guidance sent to managers: baseline pool = 6% of payroll for ICs, 8% for managers (typical orgs). final amounts vary by business performance — comp committee will publish final %. expect announcement with final % before calibration.
Jonah (Recruiter): if a candidate is converted from contractor to FTE during the cycle, do they become eligible?
Maya (People Ops): converted hires are eligible if converted before the cutoff and have 6 months tenure as an employee (not contractor). short conversions can be escalated to exceptions.
HR Bot: Reminder: Open enrollment Q&A session tomorrow 11am PT  link: https://meet.redwood/hr/enroll :calendar:
Alec (Eng): parental leave question: does parental leave affect review eligibility or timeline? one of my directs went on leave last quarter.
Maya (People Ops): parental leave pauses the review clock for tenure-based eligibility but performance evidence still counts. managers should document impact and include return-to-work plan in the packet. we will flag these for the panel.
Priya (SWE): appeals process? someone asked if they can appeal a level decision more than once.
Maya (People Ops): appeals: single formal appeal per cycle. steps: 1) manager+IC meet; 2) submit appeal form within 7 business days; 3) panel review within 10 business days. appeals are for process or missing evidence, not re-litigating subjective judgments.
Laila (Manager): is there a checklist for managers preparing packets? saves us time.
Maya (People Ops): yes  manager checklist (pasteable):
```
- employee_name
- current_level + proposed_level
- 3 concise evidence bullets (impact, scope, leader feedback)
- previous_review_summary (if any)
- comp_request or band_adjustment
- manager_signoff + peer_feedback links
```
Maya (People Ops): please use that exact format to avoid back-and-forth.
Jonah (Recruiter): small note on promotions + external offers: do we counter-offer during cycle?
Maya (People Ops): we can make offers but compensation adjustments tied to the cycle won't process until effective date. for urgent retention cases, reach out to recruiting+people ops for a retention pay recommendation.
Alec (Eng): effective date question: if approval happens the last day of month, is effective next day or start of next month?
Maya (People Ops): effective date = first of next month unless payroll needs a manual retro. we prefer the clean first-of-month.
Priya (SWE): anything new on leveling examples? people asked for concrete L4 vs L5 examples.
Maya (People Ops): added three new examples per level in rubric v2 (project scope, cross-team influence, mentoring). link in notes.
Maya (People Ops): final: i'll post a short FAQ in #announcements and send managers a calibration prep pack. DM me for 1:1s or specific edge cases. thanks!
